samples.summary: The CLI's 30-second callback timeout was not revisited even though the backend now inserts a mandatory human consent interstitial into the CLI login flow
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer` still rejects with `Login timed out` after `30_000` ms (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:451 — code the diff did not touch). The backend side of this change (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:226 → `req.__cliConsent`, rendered by `AuthController.renderCliConsent`) now stops a `mode=cli` start *before* GitHub and requires the person to read an interstitial and click "Continue sign-in", on top of GitHub's own consent screen. The whole human sequence — browser launch, read interstitial, click, GitHub authorize — must now complete inside 30 s or the CLI aborts and the code never arrives. The server's own budget for the same human step is 5 minutes (`STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS`, github-auth.guard.ts, and the 5-min `CliAuthStore` state TTL), so the two ends now disagree by an order of magnitude. docs/design/cli.md:205 and :282 still document the 30-second timeout as the flow's budget, i.e. the doc was updated for the new interstitial but the timeout was left as-is. Fix belongs on the CLI timeout (raise it toward the server's 5-minute state TTL).

samples.summary: Both login flows write the same single `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie, so a second login start in the same browser silently invalidates the first
samples.evidence: `issueLoginCookie(context, OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE)` is called for the CLI branch (github-auth.guard.ts:241) and for the browser branch (github-auth.guard.ts:250) with one fixed name and `path: '/'`. Any second start overwrites the first browser's half, and `AuthController.takeStateCookie` (auth.controller.ts, `res.clearCookie` on read) makes it single-use. Reachable out-of-diff entry point: the frontend's plain sign-in link at packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:53 (`${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/github`) — a user who has a `wafflebase login` waiting on the consent page and then clicks Sign in in another tab (or simply double-clicks/reloads the login link) clobbers the cookie, so the earlier callback is refused: `400 CLI login state expired` for the CLI, or `/login?error=login_state` for the browser. Before this change concurrent/retried starts were harmless because no cookie existed. A per-login cookie name (or a small set) would remove the collision.

samples.summary: Backend README's "Auth Flow" still describes the pre-change callback (no `state`, no cookie validation, no CLI consent page)
samples.evidence: packages/backend/README.md:387-399 lists the flow as "Frontend links to GET /auth/github → Passport redirects to GitHub → callback → findOrCreateUser → cookies", with no mention of the `state` the guard now always mints, the `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie, the `/login?error=login_state` failure redirect, or the CLI consent interstitial. `docs/design/backend.md:103-144` and `docs/design/cli.md` were updated; this README consumer was not. (Package READMEs are not covered by the top-level design-doc link check.)

samples.summary: Already-published CLI versions can no longer log in against an upgraded backend (hard version-skew break)
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.ts:209/219 now throws `BadRequestException` for any `mode=cli` start lacking `nonce`/`code_challenge`. The only in-repo producer (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:57) is updated in lockstep, but any `@wafflebase/cli` build already installed by a user constructs `"/auth/github?mode=cli&port="` alone and will now receive a 400 on every `wafflebase login`. The tradeoff is deliberate and stated in the guard's class comment and docs/design/cli.md:273-283; flagging only because the break lands on out-of-repo consumers and may warrant a release note / minimum-CLI-version check rather than a bare 400.

finding.evidence: `startCallbackServer` still rejects with `Login timed out` after `30_000` ms (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:451 — code the diff did not touch). The backend side of this change (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:226 → `req.__cliConsent`, rendered by `AuthController.renderCliConsent`) now stops a `mode=cli` start *before* GitHub and requires the person to read an interstitial and click "Continue sign-in", on top of GitHub's own consent screen. The whole human sequence — browser launch, read interstitial, click, GitHub authorize — must now complete inside 30 s or the CLI aborts and the code never arrives. The server's own budget for the same human step is 5 minutes (`STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS`, github-auth.guard.ts, and the 5-min `CliAuthStore` state TTL), so the two ends now disagree by an order of magnitude. docs/design/cli.md:205 and :282 still document the 30-second timeout as the flow's budget, i.e. the doc was updated for the new interstitial but the timeout was left as-is. verdict.reason: Every claimed element is present as described. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:436-451 arms a fixed 30_000 ms timer inside startCallbackServer's promise constructor — before srv.listen (line 457) and before openBrowser (line 70) — and nothing resets it; the /launch/<token> handler (lines 342-364) redirects without touching it, so the entire human sequence must finish in 30 s. The backend now interposes a mandatory human interstitial into this exact mode=cli path: github-auth.guard.ts:226-235 sets req.__cliConsent and returns true before super.canActivate (line 257) whenever hasConfirmation (lines 261-272) is false, and auth.controller.ts:118-125 renders it via renderCliConsent (line 144); hasConfirmation requires a query param matching a cookie, obtainable only by a human click, with no auto-continue. The server's budget for the same step is 5 minutes (github-auth.guard.ts:35 STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS, applied at line 293; cli-auth.store.ts:70 state TTL), an order of magnitude larger. docs/design/cli.md:205 and :282 still document the 30-second timeout. Additional corroboration: login.ts:231 tells headless users the login URL "expires in 5 minutes" while the same process aborts at 30 s, so the CLI already self-contradicts. This is in-lane for blast-radius (a behaviour change on one side of a cross-package flow leaving an unchanged consumer's timing contract broken, at a site the diff does not show) and the impact is a reachable failure of the primary login path, matching major. No guard, retry, or timer extension elsewhere mitigates it.

finding.evidence: `issueLoginCookie(context, OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE)` is called for the CLI branch (github-auth.guard.ts:241) and for the browser branch (github-auth.guard.ts:250) with one fixed name and `path: '/'`. Any second start overwrites the first browser's half, and `AuthController.takeStateCookie` (auth.controller.ts, `res.clearCookie` on read) makes it single-use. Reachable out-of-diff entry point: the frontend's plain sign-in link at packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:53 (`${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/github`) — a user who has a `wafflebase login` waiting on the consent page and then clicks Sign in in another tab (or simply double-clicks/reloads the login link) clobbers the cookie, so the earlier callback is refused: `400 CLI login state expired` for the CLI, or `/login?error=login_state` for the browser. verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE` is a single fixed name (github-auth.guard.ts:17) written with `path: '/'` (loginCookieOptions, :68-75) by both the CLI branch (:241) and the browser branch (:250) via `issueLoginCookie`, which unconditionally overwrites any existing value (:282-296). `AuthController.takeStateCookie` (auth.controller.ts:322-327) reads and clears it in one step, and both callback validations depend on the exact value: browser signature compare at :279-287 (→ `/login?error=login_state` via :210-212) and CLI `secretEquals(state.browserBinding, binding)` at :294-308 (→ 400 'CLI login state expired or invalid'). Out-of-diff entry points that reach a second start with no namespacing or dedup are real: packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:53 and packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:57. No guard anywhere checks for a pre-existing state cookie; `hasConfirmation` (:261-272) only covers the separate CLI_CONFIRM_COOKIE. This is a shared-state invariant violated by out-of-diff consumers, squarely in the blast-radius lane, with real login-failure impact.
